caseFields.help: Used in the discordance comment when a part is marked as not representing the cytology lesion.

options.label: Case summary line after the diagnosis (highest grade lesion and parts)

fields.label: Polyp type
fields.help: Decidual: stroma decidualised in pregnancy or with progestogens. Endometrial: endometrial-type glands and stroma (lower uterine segment, or a prolapsed endometrial polyp).

fields.label: Tissue present
options: Detached squamous epithelium and endocervical fragments

fields.label: Curettings contain
options: Endocervical mucosa with detached squamous fragments

reference.title: Cervical squamous lesions
reference.intro: Two tiers, LSIL and HSIL, with the CIN grade in brackets; block-type p16 supports HSIL when CIN II is in question.

groups.heading: Negative
points: Orderly maturation from a single basal layer to flattened surface cells

images.caption: Normal ectocervical squamous epithelium (H&E).
images.credit: Ed Uthman, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

groups.heading: LSIL (CIN I)
points: Maturation preserved, with atypia and mitoses limited to the lower third
Koilocytes in the upper layers: enlarged, hyperchromatic, irregular nuclei with perinuclear halos
p16 usually negative or weak and patchy, but overexpressed in about a third: only a negative or patchy result helps

images.caption: Cervical LSIL (CIN I) on the left beside normal squamous epithelium on the right (H&E).
images.credit: Ed Uthman, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

images.caption: Cervical LSIL (CIN I): koilocytes in the upper layers with preserved maturation (H&E).
images.credit: Ed Uthman, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

groups.heading: HSIL (CIN II)
points: Atypia and mitoses into the middle third, with maturation of the upper third
Strong, diffuse block p16 supports HSIL

images.caption: Cervical biopsy at 12 o'clock showing CIN II (HSIL) (H&E).
images.credit: Ed Uthman, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

groups.heading: HSIL (CIN III)
points: Basal and parabasal-type cells through the full thickness, without maturation
Thin HSIL (fewer than 10 cells thick) can mimic atrophy: p16 separates them

images.caption: CIN III (HSIL) in a cervical biopsy: basal-type cells through the full thickness, without maturation (H&E).
images.credit: Ed Uthman, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

images.caption: CIN III: atypical cells with nuclear pleomorphism through a little more than two-thirds of the epithelium (H&E).
images.credit: Mikael Häggström, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

reference.title: Vaginal squamous lesions
reference.intro: Graded by the depth of atypia, as in the cervix: VaIN 1 is LSIL, and VaIN 2 and VaIN 3 are HSIL.

groups.heading: LSIL (VaIN 1)
points: Atypia in the lower third, with koilocytes towards the surface
p16 focal or weak

groups.heading: HSIL (VaIN 2)
points: Atypia in the lower two-thirds, with maturation of the upper third

groups.heading: HSIL (VaIN 3)
points: Atypia in more than two-thirds, including full thickness carcinoma in situ
p16 block-type beyond the lower third in nearly all high grade lesions; p53 wild-type
Check the basement membrane to exclude invasion

images.caption: VaIN 3: a full thickness intraepithelial lesion with severe dysplasia (H&E).
images.credit: Bruno et al., Cancers (Basel) 2024, Fig 1, full figure

reference.note: Room for your own photographs of VaIN 1 and VaIN 2: no openly licensed images of either were found.

fields.label: Squamous epithelium
fields.help: Differentiated VIN is HPV-independent, with basal atypia only, and is never called HSIL.

reference.title: Vulval squamous lesions
reference.intro: Two pathways: HPV-associated LSIL and HSIL, and HPV-independent differentiated VIN, whose atypia is basal and which is never called HSIL.

groups.heading: LSIL
points: Acanthosis or papillomatosis with koilocytes in the upper layers
Mild atypia and mitoses limited to the lower third; binucleate cells
p16 usually negative; Ki-67 raised mainly in the lower third

groups.heading: LSIL (condyloma acuminatum)
points: Papillary acanthosis with hyperkeratosis and prominent koilocytes
Prints as LSIL with condyloma acuminatum in brackets
A fibroepithelial stromal polyp has no papillomatosis or koilocytes

images.caption: Vulval condyloma acuminatum: acanthotic squamous epithelium with prominent koilocytes (H&E).
images.credit: Léonard et al., Biomed Res Int 2014, Fig 1, full figure

images.caption: Condyloma acuminatum: koilocytes with perinuclear halos and enlarged, wrinkled nuclei in the upper layers (H&E).
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

groups.heading: HSIL (usual-type VIN)
points: Atypical nuclei in all layers, including the middle and upper thirds, with suprabasal and atypical mitoses
Warty type: surface keratosis, koilocytes and wide rete; basaloid type: immature parabasal-type cells throughout
Often extends into hair follicles and skin appendages; p16 block-type, p53 wild-type

images.caption: Vulval HSIL, basaloid type: atypical parabasal-type cells through nearly the whole thickness of the epidermis (H&E).
images.credit: Léonard et al., Biomed Res Int 2014, Fig 3, full figure

images.caption: Vulval HSIL (VIN III in the older terms): atypia through the full thickness with loss of maturation (H&E).
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

groups.heading: Differentiated VIN (HPV-independent)
points: Acanthosis, parakeratosis and elongated, anastomosing rete ridges
Atypia confined to the basal and parabasal layers: enlarged cells with eosinophilic cytoplasm, vesicular nuclei, prominent nucleoli and prominent intercellular bridges
p53 mutant-type (basal, diffuse, null or cytoplasmic); p16 negative or patchy; can be hard to separate from lichen simplex chronicus in a punch biopsy

images.caption: Differentiated VIN at low power: acanthosis and parakeratosis with elongated, anastomosing rete ridges (H&E).
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

images.caption: Differentiated VIN, deep epithelium: enlarged eosinophilic keratinocytes with atypical basal nuclei (H&E).
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons (cropped)

images.caption: Differentiated VIN: atypical keratinocytes with large vesicular nuclei and macronucleoli in the basal and mid layers, without koilocytes (H&E).
images.credit: Léonard et al., Biomed Res Int 2014, Fig 4, full figure

groups.heading: Squamous cell carcinoma
points: Desmoplasia, irregular contours, an inflammatory response and distorted architecture
Block-type p16 is a reliable surrogate for HPV-associated carcinoma

images.caption: Keratinising squamous cell carcinoma of the vulva: infiltrating mature cells with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm and keratin pearls (H&E).
images.credit: Léonard et al., Biomed Res Int 2014, Fig 6, full figure

reference.note: Room for your own photographs of flat vulval LSIL: no openly licensed image of it was found.

fields.label: HPV status
fields.help: Block-type p16 is the usual surrogate for an HPV-associated carcinoma.

reference.title: Paget disease
reference.intro: Large pale cells in the epidermis; stains separate primary Paget disease from pagetoid spread of an anorectal or urothelial carcinoma.

groups.heading: Primary, intraepithelial
points: Enlarged polygonal cells with abundant pale cytoplasm, large nuclei and small to prominent nucleoli; intracytoplasmic mucin is frequent
Mainly basal and parabasal, extending upwards singly and in small clusters, often into skin adnexa
Basal keratinocytes are preserved but may be compressed

images.caption: Extramammary Paget disease in a vulval biopsy: large cells with pale cytoplasm in the epidermis (H&E).
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

images.caption: Primary extramammary Paget disease of the vulva: pale Paget cells scattered through the epidermis (H&E).
images.credit: Sarahkayb, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

groups.heading: Primary, with dermal invasion
points: Single cells or small groups infiltrating the dermis with a desmoplastic reaction

groups.heading: Secondary (pagetoid spread)
points: Anorectal primary: CK20, CDX2 and SATB2 positive; CK7, GATA3 and GCDFP-15 usually negative
Urothelial primary: CK7, CK20, GATA3, uroplakin III and p63 positive; GCDFP-15 negative

reference.note: Room for your own photographs of invasive and secondary Paget disease: no openly licensed images of either were found.

reference.title: Paget disease stains
reference.intro: Primary Paget cells are CK7, GATA3, CEA and GCDFP-15 positive, and CK20, p63 and SOX10 negative.

groups.heading: CK7 positive
points: Strong in primary Paget cells; also positive in urothelial secondary spread

images.caption: Primary vulval Paget disease: the Paget cells are strongly positive (CK7 immunostain).
images.credit: Sarahkayb, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

groups.heading: GATA3 positive
points: Positive in primary and urothelial secondary disease; negative in anorectal secondary disease

images.caption: Primary vulval Paget disease: nuclear staining of the Paget cells (GATA3 immunostain).
images.credit: Sarahkayb, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

groups.heading: CEA positive
points: Positive in primary and secondary disease

images.caption: Primary vulval Paget disease: the Paget cells are positive (CEA immunostain).
images.credit: Sarahkayb, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

groups.heading: CK20 negative
points: Negative in primary disease; positive in anorectal and urothelial secondary disease

images.caption: Primary vulval Paget disease: the Paget cells are negative (CK20 immunostain).
images.credit: Sarahkayb, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

groups.heading: p63 negative
points: The Paget cells are negative among the stained keratinocytes; positive in urothelial secondary disease

images.caption: Primary vulval Paget disease: the keratinocyte nuclei stain and the Paget cells do not (p63 immunostain).
images.credit: Sarahkayb, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

reference.title: p16 patterns
reference.intro: Only strong, diffuse, continuous block staining counts as positive; patchy or mosaic staining does not support HSIL.

groups.heading: Block positive
points: Strong, continuous nuclear or nuclear and cytoplasmic staining from the basal layer upwards
Cervix: through at least the lower third; vagina: beyond the lower third
Supports HSIL and HPV-associated carcinoma

images.caption: CIN II (HSIL): strong, diffuse block staining; benign cervical biopsies often stain weakly or patchily (p16 immunostain).
images.credit: Ed Uthman, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

images.caption: HSIL: block-type p16 staining from the basal layer upwards (p16 immunostain).
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

groups.heading: Patchy / focal
points: Discontinuous, mosaic staining of variable intensity
LSIL, reactive and metaplastic epithelium, and HPV-independent lesions

images.caption: HPV-independent vulval squamous cell carcinoma: mosaic, non-block p16 staining (p16 immunostain).
images.credit: Haddad et al., Einstein (Sao Paulo) 2025, Fig 3, panel A (cropped)

groups.heading: Negative
points: No staining, or only rare scattered cells
Differentiated VIN is negative or patchy

reference.note: Room for your own photographs of p16-negative epithelium: no openly licensed image of it was found.

fields.label: Ki-67
options: Confined to the basal and parabasal layers

reference.title: Ki-67 patterns
reference.intro: Read it with p16: Ki-67 alone is raised in both low and high grade lesions.

groups.heading: Extends into the upper two-thirds
points: Positive nuclei in the middle and upper layers in HSIL
Metaplastic epithelium should not stain in the upper half

images.caption: Cervical biopsy: Ki-67-positive nuclei extending into the upper half of the epithelium, where metaplastic epithelium should not stain (Ki-67 immunostain).
images.credit: Ed Uthman, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

groups.heading: Confined to the basal and parabasal layers
points: Normal, atrophic and reactive epithelium, and lichen simplex chronicus
Differentiated VIN often stays basal, so this pattern does not exclude it

reference.note: Room for your own photographs of a basal Ki-67 pattern: no openly licensed image of it was found.

reference.title: p53 patterns
reference.intro: Six patterns in two classes; read the basal layer first. HPV-associated HSIL and lichen sclerosus are wild-type; a mutant-type pattern supports differentiated VIN.

groups.heading: Wild-type: scattered
points: Scattered nuclear staining of variable intensity in the basal and parabasal cells

images.caption: Vulval squamous cell carcinoma: scattered nuclear staining of variable intensity, a wild-type pattern (p53 immunostain).
images.credit: Kortekaas et al., Histopathology 2020, Fig 1, panel A (cropped)

groups.heading: Wild-type: mid-epithelial, basal sparing
points: Strong to moderate staining of the middle layers, sparing the basal layer
Associated with HPV

images.caption: Vulval squamous cell carcinoma: mid-epithelial staining with sparing of the basal layer, a wild-type pattern (p53 immunostain).
images.credit: Kortekaas et al., Histopathology 2020, Fig 1, panel B (cropped)

groups.heading: Mutant-type: basal overexpression
points: Strong nuclear staining of consecutive basal cells; a little parabasal staining is acceptable

images.caption: Vulval squamous cell carcinoma: strong staining of consecutive basal cells, a mutant-type pattern (p53 immunostain).
images.credit: Kortekaas et al., Histopathology 2020, Fig 1, panel C (cropped)

images.caption: Differentiated VIN: strong, continuous staining of the basal and parabasal layers, a mutant-type pattern (p53 immunostain).
images.credit: Dasgupta et al., Histopathology 2026, Fig 3, panel D (cropped)

groups.heading: Mutant-type: diffuse overexpression
points: Strong, diffuse staining of the basal and upper layers
Parabasal overexpression in more than 10 per cent of the lesion makes a basal pattern diffuse

images.caption: Vulval squamous cell carcinoma: strong staining from the basal into the upper layers, a mutant-type pattern (p53 immunostain).
images.credit: Kortekaas et al., Histopathology 2020, Fig 1, panel D (cropped)

groups.heading: Mutant-type: null
points: No nuclear staining, with a positive internal control

images.caption: Vulval squamous cell carcinoma: no nuclear staining in the tumour with positive stromal cells, a mutant-type null pattern (p53 immunostain).
images.credit: Kortekaas et al., Histopathology 2020, Fig 1, panel E (cropped)

groups.heading: Mutant-type: cytoplasmic
points: Diffuse cytoplasmic staining, with or without nuclear staining, and a positive internal control

images.caption: Vulval squamous cell carcinoma: diffuse cytoplasmic staining, a mutant-type pattern (p53 immunostain).
images.credit: Kortekaas et al., Histopathology 2020, Fig 1, panel F (cropped)

reference.title: Vulval dermatoses and benign lesions
reference.intro: The papillary dermis and the basal layer separate the three lichens; consider differentiated VIN in any of them.

groups.heading: Lichen sclerosus
points: Vacuolar interface change with homogenised, hyalinised collagen between the infiltrate and the epithelium
Hyperkeratosis, a thin epidermis with loss of rete, and band-like chronic inflammation
Early lesions may show inflammation without sclerosis and are not diagnostic; p53 wild-type

images.caption: Lichen sclerosus: a pale, homogenised papillary dermis with follicular plugging (H&E).
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

groups.heading: Lichen simplex chronicus
points: Compact hyperkeratosis, hypergranulosis and irregular acanthosis
Vertically oriented, thickened collagen bundles in the superficial dermis; no basal damage or sclerosis

images.caption: Lichen simplex chronicus: irregular psoriasiform hyperplasia with hyperkeratosis (H&E).
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

groups.heading: Lichen planus
points: Band-like lymphocytic infiltrate directly under the epithelium, with no separating sclerosis
Basal damage with Civatte bodies; saw-toothed rete in keratinised skin

images.caption: Lichen planus: a band of lymphocytes along the junction with loss of basal cells (H&E).
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

images.caption: A Civatte body (arrow): an apoptotic keratinocyte at the junction in interface dermatitis (H&E).
images.credit: Kaira et al., Ann Pathol Lab Med 2019, via Wikimedia Commons, full figure

groups.heading: Fibroepithelial stromal polyp
points: Polypoid, non-circumscribed stroma reaching the epithelial interface
Stellate and multinucleate stromal cells, often around vessels, which are not sarcoma
No papillomatosis or koilocytes, unlike condyloma

images.caption: Fibroepithelial stromal polyp of the vulva at low power: a polypoid, loose oedematous stroma under squamous epithelium (H&E).
images.credit: Amarvinita, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

images.caption: Fibroepithelial stromal polyp of the vulva: multinucleate atypical stromal cells, which are not sarcoma (H&E).
images.credit: Amarvinita, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

groups.heading: Hidradenoma papilliferum
points: Circumscribed dermal maze of papillae, cysts and glands, rarely connected to the epidermis
Luminal apocrine columnar cells over a myoepithelial layer

images.caption: Hidradenoma papilliferum in a vulval punch biopsy: a circumscribed dermal nodule of branching papillae and glands (H&E).
images.credit: Ed Uthman, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

reference.title: Benign vaginal findings
reference.intro: Thin HSIL can mimic atrophy, and a fibroepithelial stromal polyp can look alarming: p16 and the stromal cells settle most cases.

groups.heading: Atrophy
points: Thin epithelium of small uniform basal-type cells with little glycogen and no maturation abnormality
Main mimic: thin HSIL; atrophy is p16 negative

images.caption: Atrophy, shown in the cervix, where it looks the same as in the vagina: thin epithelium of small uniform cells; this case was p16 negative (H&E).
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

groups.heading: Fibroepithelial stromal polyp
points: Stellate and multinucleate stromal cells near the epithelial interface and around vessels
Desmin, ER and PR positive; no koilocytes

images.caption: Fibroepithelial stromal polyp of the vulva at low power: a polypoid, loose oedematous stroma under squamous epithelium (H&E).
images.credit: Amarvinita, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

images.caption: Fibroepithelial stromal polyp of the vulva: multinucleate atypical stromal cells, which are not sarcoma (H&E).
images.credit: Amarvinita, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

groups.heading: Vaginal adenosis
points: Mucinous (most) or tuboendometrial glands in the lamina propria or on the surface
Squamous metaplasia is how adenosis heals
Endometriosis has endometrial stroma; mesonephric remnants have dense luminal secretions

images.caption: Vaginal adenosis: tuboendometrial-type glands in the lamina propria, partly replaced by squamous metaplasia (H&E).
images.credit: National Cancer Institute, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

groups.heading: Gartner duct cyst
points: A single layer of cuboidal to low columnar non-mucinous epithelium

images.caption: Gartner duct cyst: the cyst wall (below) under the native vaginal squamous epithelium (top) (H&E).
images.credit: Ed Uthman, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

groups.heading: Müllerian cyst
points: Mucinous or ciliated tubal-type columnar lining, sometimes with squamous metaplasia

reference.note: Room for your own photographs of a Müllerian cyst: no openly licensed image of one was found.
